LESSON: WORDS WITH MIXED ACCENT MARKS • ELEVE • DEJA • COTE • THETA.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: French Braille Notation
Topic 9.1: Words with Mixed Accent Marks • Eleve • Deja • Cote • Theta.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Words with Mixed Accent Marks • Eleve • Deja • Cote • Theta., part of French Braille Notation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use accent marks in French braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. manipulate embossed Braille flashcards showing different French accent marks and match accent mark symbols to their names and sounds using a tactile matching game,

2. sort the words into categories based on accent types (acute, grave, circumflex, cedilla, diaeresis) and construct braille word cards containing mixed French accent marks (forêt, école, élève, garçon, naïf),

3. tactually read French Braille words with mixed accents following guidance on correct French pronunciation and intonation from the teacher,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. manipulate embossed Braille flashcards showing different French accent marks and match accent mark symbols to their names and sounds using a tactile matching game,
2. sort the words into categories based on accent types (acute, grave, circumflex, cedilla, diaeresis) and construct braille word cards containing mixed French accent marks (forêt, école, élève, garçon, naïf),
3. tactually read French Braille words with mixed accents following guidance on correct French pronunciation and intonation from the teacher,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Words with Mixed Accent Marks • Eleve • Deja • Cote • Theta. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Imagination and Creativity: the learner composes original Braille sentences or short texts using French words with accent

marks, demonstrating creativity in vocabulary use.

● Digital Literacy: the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology in reading and writing words with French accent

marks.

Values:
Integrity: the learner exhibits honesty in peer assessments and feedback, ensuring truthful and respectful correction of errors.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Support: the learner guides others to read prepared Braille word lists containing various accent-marked German words.
